- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overestimates continuation; reduce forecast slope in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.36) and price is trending up, model frequently over-optimistic; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent peak unless sentiment sustains.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 3–5 day horizons when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; add 1–2% upward bias for 30d forecasts if sentiment <0.25.
- When sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model often fails to recognize reversal; delay forecast drop by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude by 10–15%.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 65% of 30d average, model tends to overpredict; apply downward bias of 1–3% if sentiment is weak or flat.
